name: Millhaven villagers (named in the girl's account)

physicalDetails.detail: The girl's Mam: breath went sweet ('pears gone brown') before she was hot; died (the shaving glass did not mist); rose in the dark. Mister Pell: second to fall sick; his house or yard is at the top of the lane ('Up toward Pell's'). Missus Hale's baby: first to fall sick (a cradle with a tucked blanket and no baby is in the house by the smithy, per Lyriel; whether it is the Hale house is not stated). The drove-way clog: a man's wooden clog stood upright in the lane mud, sucked down to the instep, the foot bare after it.

goalsAtChapterEnd.active: Not applicable. Most are dead and have risen and walked out; fates not confirmed individually.

decisionsThisChapter.detail: Da: told the girl to bolt the hatch 'Not for anybody. Not if it was him'; put her down the cellar and, apparently, went out of his own door into the dark (his fate is unknown).
Mam and Da quarrelled over the newer grain seller because he was cheaper than Mister Hollis (the girl's account).
Gran Ottley came to sit with Mam; the tinker came for the pot; the newer grain seller came to the house in the last days.

knowledge.detail: Order of sickness: Missus Hale's baby, Mister Pell, then everybody coughing at the well. Sweetness of breath preceded fever. The village had a rival pair of grain sellers: Mister Hollis (established) and a newer, cheaper man.

arc.currentPosition: Presumed among the sixty-plus dead who walked up the cow way. Mister Hollis is the established grain seller whom the newer man undercuts; neither seller is seen on the page.
